title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating autonomously with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a gap between what an autonomous system detects as an obstacle worthy of reaction and what humans expect it to recognize and avoid, even when a human monitor is in the vehicle.

The company disputed whether the vehicle failed to follow traffic rules at the scene, stating it had stopped appropriately at relevant intersections. Avride responded by excluding certain streets from its service area and conducting simulated experiments to improve performance. It is not established what the vehicle's sensors detected, whether the human operator could have intervened, or what threshold of detection and response would have prevented the strike.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern about self-driving car safety. A resident reported on a neighborhood Facebook group that the vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The duck, which residents recognized because it was nesting near a local Italian restaurant, had become familiar to the community, intensifying their reaction to the incident.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously when the collision occurred. The company disputed a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it reviewed vehicle data and found appropriate stops at all relevant intersections. In response, Avride adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar incidents while ensuring safety performance remains unaffected. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
